# Research intraday small-target strategies with causal no-trade rules

## Problem and scope

The owner requested on 2026-10-23 a profitable day-trading candidate from latest
main in an isolated worktree, favouring frequent smaller wins on gold or FX,
with observable rules for when not to trade. A modest profit factor and some
losing years are acceptable. This is a new bounded study, separate from the
three rejected momentum hypotheses recorded by HT-315 and all active producer
language work. Backtests cannot establish future profitability.

## Claim — 2026-10-23 small-target research

Owner: Codex. Branch: `codex/daytrade-regime-research`, main base
`35cd03c645f88bea4ac4b4113de935ad1cea597c`.
Write scope: `scripts/research/daytrade-regime/`,
`test/daytradeRegime.test.mjs`, `docs/research/daytrade-regime/`,
`strategies/evidence/daytrade-regime/`, and immutable
`.project-memory/tasks/HT-323/` records. Scratch studies stay outside registration.
Luna helper reviews existing evidence read-only; parent owns all writes.
No existing engine, strategy registry, book, generated atlas, or other owner's
evidence paths may change without a prospective scope update. No live orders,
deployment, credentials, or external paid services are needed.

## Acceptance

- Review prior art and log all tested hypotheses and variants.
- Freeze a chronological development/test split before new outcomes.
- Use completed-bar signals, explicit execution and costs, intraday exits,
  and no filters selected from future outcomes.
- Report hit rate, trade frequency, realistic and stressed cost results,
  year splits, drawdown, losing streaks, and sensitivity to nearby settings.
- Compare the no-trade rule with the ungated baseline and inspect skipped periods.
- Retain runnable candidate and evidence if justified; do not publish a failed
  test as a finished strategy or change book membership.

## Validation

Focused causal/execution tests, reproducible historical runs, `pnpm test` for
strategy or money logic changes, `git diff --check`, and project-memory
validation on the committed implementation head. Record exact commands and
limitations after running them.

## Integration

Research only. Any implementation PR must link this task and retain the full
search record. Forward testing and book membership are separate decisions.

The isolated study has a positive USDJPY Tokyo-fix candidate. Extend this

## Review handoff — 2026-10-23

Implementation: [app PR539](https://github.com/spik3r/heisentick/pull/539),
commit `9e7e3857f9cc0e7d69ae17fbe167aa7744f99e5f`. Research editing is
finished and the claim is released for review; no merge or forward operation
is claimed. The owner/reviewer can assess the evidence before any new paper
implementation or book proposal.

The fixed USDJPY settlement-day short has 388 trades, 57.2% wins and PF 1.59
after an assumed 1.5-pip round-trip cost; PF is 1.44 at 2 pips. The final
2025–September 2026 partition has PF 1.34, while partial 2026 alone loses
82.4 pips (4.12R). Non-settlement weekdays lose money (PF 0.85); five minutes
of entry delay removes the edge. Frequency is about 1.3 trades per week.
Known prior history prevents a pristine out-of-sample claim. This is a
positive historical watch candidate with executable live profitability unproven.

Retained evidence: 48 rejected indicator route cells, two Tokyo-fix
candidates and 14 diagnostic configurations; exact trade ledgers, costs,
calendar source, monthly-block bootstrap and source/input hashes. Seven
outputs reproduced exactly with the final source, and Luna independently
recalculated the statistics and checked the final note.

## Claim — 2026-10-23 runnable scheduled strategy

The owner now requests the exact DSL and everything needed to run it. Codex
resumes this task for a scheduled-trade family and a watch strategy in the
app backtester, with the existing Luna helper providing independent review.
The research rules stay fixed. No live broker orders or deployed-book change.

Producer scope (`spik3r/heisentick-strat`, branch
`codex/scheduled-calendar-trade`): new scheduled-trade parser, config and
engine files; the minimal parser/family/run/fixture/WASM dispatch seams;
calendar data with explicit coverage; spec, manifest/generated grammar,
conformance fixtures and tests; changelog and release qualification. Existing
families retain their contracts. Use the shared broker cost and sizing rules;
compare native output with the research ledger and report any fill-cost change.

App scope (`codex/daytrade-regime-research`, existing PR539): canonical
`strategies/source/dslTokyoFixSettlementFade.strat`, its generated wrapper,
registry/library metadata; a dedicated pinned Go/WASM scheduled-trade route,
asset build/fetch and local replay command; narrow data-worker, strategy
routing and catalog seams; focused tests and browser verification; the
existing research evidence/index paths and HT-323 memory. Prefer a separate
feature release pin to overlapping the global v0.38 adoption in app PR511.
Do not change PR511's files or claim its generic runtime qualification.
Record exact final maintained paths in implementation memory before completion.

Acceptance: exact scheduled-open entry at 00:55 UTC, 20-pip stop anchored to
actual fill, 01:30 UTC exit; settlement-day weekend rollback and Japanese
holiday exclusions; fail closed outside reviewed calendar coverage; no future
bar availability used for entry admission; costed execution tests, native and
WASM parity, app strategy selection and a reproducible historical run.
A reviewed producer PR and immutable release precede the consumer pin.
